1.en: You will hear a man asking a friend for advice on things to do in the city with a family of visitors.
1.zh: 你會聽到一位男士向朋友詢問，有親戚一家來訪時在城裡可以安排哪些活動。

1.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.
1.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 1 至 6 題。

1.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.
1.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 1 至 6 題。

1.en: MAN: Sandra – I seem to remember you had some family visitors staying with you recently.
1.zh: 男士：Sandra——我記得你最近好像有家人來你那裡住過。

1.en: SANDRA: Yeah that's right. My brother and his family were here a couple of months ago.
1.zh: Sandra：是的，沒錯。我哥哥和他的家人幾個月前來過。

1.en: MAN: OK good. Well I wanted to ask your advice – I've got my cousin and her family visiting next month and as I don't have kids I've no idea where to take them.
1.zh: 男士：好，那太好了。我想問問你的建議——我表妹和她一家下個月要來，因為我沒有小孩，所以完全不知道該帶他們去哪裡。

1.en: SANDRA: Right. What about accommodation? Are they going to stay with you in your flat?
1.zh: Sandra：明白。那住宿呢？他們會住在你的公寓裡嗎？

1.en: MAN: No, thankfully – there wouldn't be room – my cousin wants me to recommend a hotel. Do you know anywhere?
1.zh: 男士：不會，幸好不會——我那裡沒有空間。我表妹想讓我推薦一家酒店。你知道哪裡合適嗎？

1.en: SANDRA: Yes, I do actually. I always recommend people stay at the Kings Hotel.
1.zh: Sandra：知道，其實我知道。我總是推薦大家住 King’s Hotel。

1.en: MAN: Where's that near?
1.zh: 男士：那附近有什麼？

1.en: SANDRA: It's about five minutes' walk from Murray Station – so nice and central. It's actually on George Street.
1.zh: Sandra：從 Murray Station 走路大約五分鐘，很方便，也在市中心。 它就在 George Street 上。

1.en: MAN: Oh yes I know. I think they're on quite a tight budget – so how much roughly is it to stay there?
1.zh: 男士：哦，是的，我知道。我想他們預算挺緊的——那住那裡大概多少錢？

1.en: SANDRA: If you book a family room it's about £125 per night.
1.zh: Sandra：如果訂家庭房，每晚大約 125 英鎊。

1.en: My brother paid for two double rooms in the end and I think that was around £95 for each room.
1.zh: 我哥哥最後訂了兩間雙人房，我記得每間大約 95 英鎊。

1.en: MAN: Oh that's not too bad.
1.zh: 男士：哦，那還不算太糟。

1.en: SANDRA: So how old are your cousin's kids?
1.zh: Sandra：那你表妹的小孩多大？

1.en: MAN: Twelve and nine. So I want to organise some trips while they're here.
1.zh: 男士：12 歲和 9 歲。所以我想在他們來的時候安排一些行程。

1.en: I was thinking of doing a bus tour of the city centre – as none of them have been here before.
1.zh: 我原本想安排市中心巴士遊，因為他們以前都沒來過這裡。

1.en: SANDRA: Those bus tours are quite expensive. I think it's better to do a walking tour – it gives you a much better feel for the city.
1.zh: Sandra：那些巴士遊挺貴的。我覺得步行導覽更好，能讓你更好地感受這座城市。

1.en: There's one that starts from Carlton Square. It takes a couple of hours and doesn't cost that much.
1.zh: 有一個導覽從 Carlton Square 出發，大約需要幾個小時，而且費用不高。

1.en: MAN: Sounds good. I'll look that up – thanks.
1.zh: 男士：聽起來不錯。我會查一下，謝謝。

1.en: SANDRA: If the weather's nice, one thing you could do is visit the old fort.
1.zh: Sandra：如果天氣好的話，你可以去參觀那座古老堡壘。

1.en: You can get there by boat. The whole trip takes half a day.
1.zh: 可以搭船去。整個行程需要半天。

1.en: MAN: That's a really good idea. I'd like to do that myself.
1.zh: 男士：這真是個好主意。我自己也想去。

1.en: And if the weather's bad I was thinking they could go to the Science Museum. But maybe they could do that when I'm at work.
1.zh: 如果天氣不好，我想他們可以去科學博物館。不過也許可以在我上班時讓他們去。

1.en: SANDRA: Yeah – don't forget it's closed on Mondays.
1.zh: Sandra：是啊——別忘了它星期一休館。

1.en: MAN: They're here from Saturday for four nights – so Tuesday would be best, I think.
1.zh: 男士：他們從星期六開始來住四晚，所以我想星期二最合適。

1.en: SANDRA: Mmm, and it won't be so crowded then. Saturdays are terrible.
1.zh: Sandra：嗯，那時也不會那麼擁擠。 星期六人非常多。

1.en: I took my kids to the exhibition on old computers there and it was far too crowded.
1.zh: 我之前帶孩子去看那裡的舊電腦展，結果太擁擠了。

1.en: I wanted to go back but it's finished now.
1.zh: 我本來還想再去一次，但現在展覽已經結束了。

1.en: MAN: That's a shame. My cousin's kids would have enjoyed that.
1.zh: 男士：真可惜。我表妹的小孩應該會喜歡那個。

1.en: SANDRA: There's another one starting soon on space which looks really good too.
1.zh: Sandra：很快會有另一個關於太空的展覽，看起來也很不錯。

1.en: MAN: OK, well I'll mention that to my cousin.
1.zh: 男士：好，我會跟我表妹提一下。

1.en: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.
1.zh: 在你聽接下來的對話之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 7 至 10 題。

1.en: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.
1.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 7 至 10 題。

1.en: SANDRA: Have you thought about where to take them to eat?
1.zh: Sandra：你有想過帶他們去哪裡吃飯嗎？

1.en: MAN: Well I really like all the food stalls at Clacton Market. My cousin's vegetarian – I know it's one of the best places for that kind of food.
1.zh: 男士：嗯，我很喜歡 Clacton Market 的那些食物攤位。我表妹吃素，我知道那裡是最適合吃這類食物的地方之一。

1.en: SANDRA: Definitely, and there'll be loads of choice for the kids, too.
1.zh: Sandra：絕對是，而且孩子們也會有很多選擇。

1.en: You need to get there quite early though – at the weekend most of the stalls stop serving lunch at 2.30.
1.zh: 不過你們得早點到——週末大多數攤位下午 2:30 就停止供應午餐了。

1.en: MAN: Good point. It's all going to need careful planning!
1.zh: 男士：說得好。這一切都得仔細規劃！

1.en: My cousin said she'd love to take the kids to a show at the theatre – but tickets are so expensive!
1.zh: 我表妹說她很想帶孩子們去劇院看演出，但票太貴了！

1.en: SANDRA: I know. But you can get some good deals if you book online with bargaintickets.com for the following day – on some seats there's a 75% discount.
1.zh: Sandra：我知道。不過如果你在 bargaintickets.com 上預訂隔天的票，可以找到一些很划算的優惠 ——有些座位有 75% 的折扣。

1.en: MAN: Really?! I must try and get some.
1.zh: 男士：真的嗎？！我一定要試著買幾張。

1.en: SANDRA: Yeah. There are lots of things you can do for free as well – no need to spend a fortune.
1.zh: Sandra：是啊。也有很多免費活動可以做，不需要花一大筆錢。

1.en: MAN: Like what?
1.zh: 男士：比如什麼？

1.en: SANDRA: They're coming next month, right?
1.zh: Sandra：他們下個月來，對吧？

1.en: Well, check and see if it's the same weekend as the Roots Music Festival in Blakewell Gardens.
1.zh: 那你查查看，是不是剛好和 Blakewell Gardens 的 Roots Music Festival 在同一個週末。

1.en: MAN: R double-O-T-S?
1.zh: 男士：R，兩個 O，T-S？

1.en: SANDRA: Yeah. Check it out online. It's always a family-friendly event and there's no entry charge.
1.zh: Sandra：是的。你可以上網查一下。 那一直都是很適合家庭參加的活動，而且不收門票。

1.en: MAN: That sounds perfect.
1.zh: 男士：聽起來很完美。

1.en: SANDRA: And if you're in Blakewell Gardens – climb Telegraph Hill – you'll be able to look right down on the port.
1.zh: Sandra：如果你們在 Blakewell Gardens，可以爬上 Telegraph Hill， 就能直接俯瞰港口。

1.en: Everyone's always really impressed because it's so huge.
1.zh: 大家總是印象很深刻，因為它實在太大了。

1.en: MAN: Oh yeah – I've been meaning to do that for ages. I've heard the view's amazing.
1.zh: 男士：哦，是啊——我一直想去那裡很久了。我聽說景色很棒。

1.en: SANDRA: Yeah. It's really worth the effort.
1.zh: Sandra：是啊，真的很值得。

1.en: MAN: Well that's given me loads of ideas. Thanks so much …
1.zh: 男士：嗯，這給了我很多想法。非常感謝……

1.en: That is the end of part one. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part one.
1.zh: 第一部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第一部分的答案。

2.en: You will hear a Guide talking to members of the public who are visiting a football stadium in the UK.
2.zh: 你會聽到一位導遊向正在參觀英國一座足球場的民眾介紹資訊。

2.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.
2.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 11 至 14 題。

2.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
2.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 11 至 14 題。

2.en: Good morning, and welcome to City Football Club.
2.zh: 早安，歡迎來到 City Football Club。

2.en: I'd like to give you some useful information about your visit to the stadium today, and then we'll start the tour of the areas of the stadium that are open to visitors.
2.zh: 我想先提供一些關於今天參觀球場的實用資訊，然後我們會開始參觀球場中對遊客開放的區域。

2.en: I can see lots of children here today, so just to let mums and dads know a few things before we start.
2.zh: 我今天看到有很多孩子在場，所以在開始前，先讓各位家長了解幾件事。

2.en: The stadium has lots of stairs, and the players' tunnel is very dark.
2.zh: 球場裡有很多樓梯，而且球員通道非常昏暗。

2.en: Please don't let your children wander off on their own, even for a minute.
2.zh: 請不要讓孩子自己走開，即使只有一分鐘也不要。

2.en: We don't want any accidents or anyone getting frightened.
2.zh: 我們不希望發生任何意外，也不希望有人受到驚嚇。

2.en: Cameras are permitted everywhere, and you can take pictures of your child shooting a penalty.
2.zh: 這裡到處都可以拍照，你們也可以拍下孩子踢點球的畫面。

2.en: Assistants are helping to organise this, and hopefully the queue won't be too long – it's very hot and sunny out on the pitch today.
2.zh: 工作人員會協助安排這項活動， 希望排隊不會太久——今天球場上非常炎熱，而且陽光很強。

2.en: You can get food and drink at the café, and I really recommend the healthy lunch boxes for children.
2.zh: 你們可以在咖啡館買食物和飲料，我非常推薦給孩子們的健康午餐盒。

2.en: Also in the café, children are invited to do a football-themed drawing.
2.zh: 另外，在咖啡館裡，孩子們也可以參加足球主題繪畫活動。

2.en: We'll pick the best one at the end of the afternoon, so don't forget to put your name and contact details on the back.
2.zh: 我們會在下午結束時選出最佳作品，所以別忘了在背面寫上姓名和聯絡方式。

2.en: That way, if you've left the stadium before then, we'll send your prize, but sadly we can't return drawings.
2.zh: 這樣，如果你們那時已經離開球場，我們會把獎品寄給你；不過很遺憾，畫作無法退還。

2.en: I'd like to mention some features of the tour.
2.zh: 我想介紹一下這次導覽的一些特色。

2.en: We'll start with the three-sixty cinema experience, which has been very popular over the years, and then I'll take you to the players' dressing rooms before going outside to the seating area and the pitch.
2.zh: 我們會從 360 度影院體驗開始， 這項體驗多年來一直很受歡迎； 之後我會帶你們去球員更衣室， 然後再到外面的座位區和球場。

2.en: I should say, if you’d prefer your visit to be self-guided, please collect headphones from the reception and then you can listen to the pre-recorded information at your own speed.
2.zh: 我也要說明一下，如果你們比較喜歡自助導覽，可以到接待處領取耳機，然後按照自己的速度收聽預錄資訊。

2.en: We've only just introduced this feature, and would appreciate your feedback.
2.zh: 我們剛推出這項功能，所以很希望得到你們的回饋。

2.en: We're thinking of offering tours in other languages in future so if you have any thoughts on that, we'd welcome those too.
2.zh: 我們正在考慮未來提供其他語言的導覽，如果你們對此有任何想法，也歡迎提出。

2.en: If you plan to return another time, you might like to book one of our VIP tours – we've only just started offering these, and they can be booked online.
2.zh: 如果你們打算下次再來，也許可以預訂我們的 VIP 導覽——這是我們剛開始提供的服務，可以在線上預訂。

2.en: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.
2.zh: 在你聽接下來的演講之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 15 至 20 題。

2.en: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.
2.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 15 至 20 題。

2.en: Now, the stadium you see today was built in 1989, as part of a three-year redevelopment project – while that project was going on, the team had to play its matches at the ground of another club – apart from that, the club has been here on this site since 1870.
2.zh: 現在你們看到的這座球場建於 1989 年，是一項為期三年的重建工程的一部分。工程進行期間， 球隊不得不在另一家俱樂部的場地比賽；除此之外，這家俱樂部自 1870 年以來一直就在這個位置。

2.en: As some of you may know, that was the start of a really important decade in the history of football in this country.
2.zh: 你們有些人可能知道，那是這個國家足球史上一個非常重要十年的開始。

2.en: For example, 1870 was also the year that football teams started to include a player whose role it was to guard the goal.
2.zh: 例如，1870 年也是足球隊開始設置一名負責守門的球員的年份。

2.en: It's hard to imagine what the game must have been like without someone in that position, isn't it?
2.zh: 很難想像沒有這個位置的比賽會是什麼樣子，不是嗎？

2.en: In 1872 and 73, many other clubs were established, both here and abroad, and the following year, in 1874, referees were allowed to send players off if they committed certain offences.
2.zh: 在 1872 年和 1873 年，國內外成立了許多其他俱樂部；接下來的 1874 年，如果球員犯下某些違規行為，裁判可以將他們罰下場。

2.en: And also in that year, teams started having to swap ends at half-time.
2.zh: 同樣在那一年，球隊開始必須在中場休息時交換場地。

2.en: One fact I was interested to discover was that in early football games, the aim was for the scorer to get the ball between two flag posts, and later between sticks joined at the top with a piece of tape.
2.zh: 我覺得很有趣的一點是，在早期足球比賽中，得分的目標是把球踢進兩根旗桿之間；後來則是在兩根頂端用膠帶連起來的木杆之間。

2.en: In 1875, that tape was replaced with the solid crossbar that we're familiar with today.
2.zh: 到 1875 年，那條膠帶被我們今天熟悉的實心橫樑取代。

2.en: 1877 saw the founding of further new clubs, and the history books tell us that in the same year, all the clubs decided to set a limit of ninety minutes for each match.
2.zh: 1877 年又有更多新俱樂部成立， 歷史書告訴我們，同年所有俱樂部決定把每場比賽時間限制為 90 分鐘。

2.en: Before that, it was a more casual arrangement, and this sometimes caused huge arguments – and sometimes fights – during matches, when one team called the end of the game and the other team wanted to play on to try and score a winning goal.
2.zh: 在那之前，比賽時間安排比較隨意，這有時會在比賽中引發激烈爭論，甚至打架；例如一隊宣布比賽結束，而另一隊想繼續比賽以爭取致勝進球。

2.en: By 1878, the number of teams in the football league increased again.
2.zh: 到 1878 年，足球聯賽中的球隊數量再次增加。

2.en: In addition, referees started using whistles, and electric lamps were installed on certain pitches.
2.zh: 此外，裁判開始使用哨子，有些球場也安裝了電燈。

2.en: This was a significant change, as games could then be played in the evenings all year round.
2.zh: 這是一項重大改變，因為這樣一來，全年晚上都可以進行比賽。

2.en: In 1880, clubs began to charge fans for admission to games, even though players were still amateurs and had other 'proper' jobs.
2.zh: 1880 年，俱樂部開始向球迷收取比賽入場費，雖然當時球員仍是業餘球員，並且有其他「正式」工作。

2.en: That's hard to imagine in the modern professional game where top players earn significant sums of money from both playing and commercial activities.
2.zh: 在現代職業足球中，頂級球員能從比賽和商業活動中賺取巨額收入，這一點很難想像。

2.en: That is the end of part two. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part two.
2.zh: 第二部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第二部分的答案。

3.en: You will hear two education students discussing an assignment on teaching handwriting to children.
3.zh: 你會聽到兩位教育系學生討論一項關於教孩子書寫的作業。

3.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
3.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 21 至 24 題。

3.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
3.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 21 至 24 題。

3.en: MAN: How are you getting on with the assignment on handwriting?
3.zh: 男士：你關於書寫的作業進行得怎麼樣？

3.en: WOMAN: Not too bad. You know, I hadn't realised that children benefit in so many ways from learning to write.
3.zh: 女士：還不錯。你知道嗎，我以前沒有意識到孩子學習書寫能有這麼多方面的好處。

3.en: It's such an important skill and yet most people think handwriting is less important than in the past because people hardly ever write by hand these days.
3.zh: 這是一項非常重要的技能，但大多數人認為手寫不如過去重要，因為現在人們幾乎不再手寫了。

3.en: MAN: Yes. And all the evidence suggests children should learn to write by hand before they learn to type. Not least because it helps their memory.
3.zh: 男士：是啊。而且所有證據都表明，孩子應該先學會手寫， 再學打字。這尤其是因為手寫有助於記憶。

3.en: WOMAN: That's right. The physical act of writing helps children to remember letters.
3.zh: 女士：沒錯。書寫這個身體動作能幫助孩子記住字母。

3.en: That seems pretty obvious when you think about it.
3.zh: 仔細想想，這似乎很明顯。

3.en: MAN: What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration.
3.zh: 男士：比較不明顯的是，它如何幫助培養專注力。

3.en: They have to sit still and focus on one thing.
3.zh: 他們必須坐好，專注在一件事上。

3.en: WOMAN: Yeah. That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before.
3.zh: 女士：是啊。我以前從沒想過手寫的這一面。

3.en: MAN: Same here. I'm not sure I understand how it improves children's imagination though.
3.zh: 男士：我也是。不過我不太確定自己是否理解它怎麼提升孩子的想像力。

3.en: WOMAN: Well, there was that study which showed that primary aged children generated more ideas when they were writing by hand than using a keyboard. I would've guessed that would be the case.
3.zh: 女士：嗯，有一項研究顯示，小學年齡的孩子手寫時，比使用鍵盤時能產生更多想法。我本來就猜會是這樣。

3.en: MAN: Mmm, yeah. I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either.
3.zh: 男士：嗯，是啊。我以前也從沒把空間感和手寫聯想到一起。

3.en: I thought spatial awareness was more to do with knowing where you are in relation to objects or other people.
3.zh: 我以為空間感更多是指知道自己相對於物體或他人的位置。

3.en: WOMAN: I thought that too. But good spatial awareness is essential for writing because you have to space words correctly.
3.zh: 女士：我也這麼以為。但良好的空間感對書寫很重要，因為你必須正確安排單字之間的距離。

3.en: It's not just fine motor skills that improve through writing as I'd always assumed.
3.zh: 書寫能提升的不只是我一直以為的精細動作能力。

3.en: MAN: Handwriting is so much harder for children with dyspraxia, who have problems coordinating movement.
3.zh: 男士：對於有動作協調障礙的孩子來說，手寫困難得多，因為他們在協調動作方面有問題。

3.en: It's good there are lots of things you can do in the classroom to help them.
3.zh: 好在課堂上有很多方法可以幫助他們。

3.en: They need so much more support with letter formation – you need to play lots of games to help them distinguish letter shapes. It takes a lot of patience.
3.zh: 他們在字母成形方面需要更多支持——你需要透過很多遊戲幫助他們區分字母形狀。這需要很大的耐心。

3.en: WOMAN: Yeah. I liked the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard.
3.zh: 女士：是啊。我很喜歡那種如果用力過大就會亮起來的筆。

3.en: That seems like a really simple solution.
3.zh: 這看起來是個非常簡單的解決辦法。

3.en: MAN: Yes, absolutely. I'm not sure there's much you can do about children with dyspraxia writing very slowly.
3.zh: 男士：是的，完全同意。至於有動作協調障礙的孩子寫得很慢，我不確定能做什麼。

3.en: It's more important to focus on accuracy and as they get more confident I think they eventually speed up.
3.zh: 更重要的是先注重準確性；等他們更有信心後，我想最終速度會提高。

3.en: WOMAN: One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper.
3.zh: 女士：有一個相當簡單的方法，就是使用方格紙。

3.en: So they write each letter in a box and that trains them to space the letters correctly.
3.zh: 讓他們把每個字母寫在一個格子裡，這樣可以訓練他們正確安排字母間距。

3.en: MAN: Indeed, that's more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line.
3.zh: 男士：確實，這比試著讓他們寫成一直線更能提升可讀性。

3.en: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
3.zh: 在你聽接下來的討論之前，你有一些時間閱讀第 25 至 30 題。

3.en: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
3.zh: 現在請聆聽並回答第 25 至 30 題。

3.en: MAN: For some children it might be better to teach them to write on a laptop rather than by hand.
3.zh: 男士：對某些孩子來說，教他們用筆電寫作可能比手寫更好。

3.en: Like children with dyslexia. They often really struggle with handwriting and some just give up.
3.zh: 例如有閱讀障礙的孩子。他們常常在手寫方面非常吃力，有些甚至直接放棄。

3.en: WOMAN: Yeah. It's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong – on a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go.
3.zh: 女士：是啊。如果寫錯了，他們不會那麼沮喪——用鍵盤時， 他們可能更願意嘗試。

3.en: But I read that developing fluency isn't any faster.
3.zh: 但我讀到過，這樣培養流暢度並不會更快。

3.en: MAN: That's right. Did you read that article on the benefits of teaching print rather than cursive handwriting, where the letters are joined up?
3.zh: 男士：沒錯。你有讀那篇關於教印刷體而不是草寫體的文章嗎？草寫體就是字母連在一起的那種。

3.en: WOMAN: Yes. Well in the past cursive writing was certainly considered more stylish and educated.
3.zh: 女士：有。以前草寫確實被認為更有風格，也更有教養。

3.en: But not anymore. Teachers' attitudes have changed because it's been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn – especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.
3.zh: 但現在不是了。教師的態度已經改變，因為事實證明草寫更難學——尤其是對有學習困難的孩子來說，把字母連起來非常有挑戰性。

3.en: MAN: I agree. I was always worried that my poor handwriting affected my exam results.
3.zh: 男士：我同意。我以前一直擔心自己糟糕的字跡會影響考試成績。

3.en: And now research shows that I was right to worry.
3.zh: 現在研究顯示，我的擔心是有道理的。

3.en: I'm sure a lot of students think it's unfair that they're being judged on their handwriting not just their knowledge.
3.zh: 我相信很多學生都覺得，考試不只評估知識，還評估字跡， 這很不公平。

3.en: WOMAN: Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script.
3.zh: 女士：如果考官看不懂答卷， 分數肯定會受到影響。

3.en: That's why it's always been so important to teach children to write legibly…
3.zh: 這就是為什麼教孩子寫得清楚易讀一直都很重要……

3.en: Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future?
3.zh: 你覺得手寫在未來的作用會改變嗎？

3.en: MAN: I can't see that changing much.
3.zh: 男士：我看不出會有太大變化。

3.en: Touch typing still isn't taught in most schools, which is a shame.
3.zh: 大多數學校仍然沒有教觸控打字，這很可惜。

3.en: But maybe that won't be necessary in the future because people will also be able to write by hand on digital devices. Anyway, teachers understand the value of handwriting. It's a basic life skill.
3.zh: 但也許未來這不會那麼必要， 因為人們也能在數位裝置上手寫。不管怎樣，老師們理解手寫的價值。它是一項基本生活技能。

3.en: WOMAN: True. However, the fact is that people are writing by hand less and less and relying on digital devices. That does cause some problems.
3.zh: 女士：沒錯。不過事實是，人們越來越少手寫，越來越依賴數位裝置。這確實造成了一些問題。

3.en: MAN: You mean like note taking? There are lots of apps for that.
3.zh: 男士：你是指像記筆記嗎？有很多應用程式可以做這個。

3.en: WOMAN: And for reading historical documents apparently.
3.zh: 女士：顯然也有用來閱讀歷史文件的。

3.en: But my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent.
3.zh: 但我媽媽對我糟糕的拼字和非常不一致的標點使用感到震驚。

3.en: I think you can put that down to lack of practice.
3.zh: 我想這可以歸因於缺乏練習。

3.en: MAN: I expect so. Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now.
3.zh: 男士：我想是這樣。就我個人而言，我很懷念手寫。我現在幾乎不寫任何東西了。

3.en: I remember my grandparents had such beautiful handwriting and it was so individual.
3.zh: 我記得我的祖父母字寫得非常漂亮，而且很有個人特色。

3.en: Nobody I know would be able to identify my handwriting now. It's a shame.
3.zh: 現在我認識的人大概沒有人能認出我的字跡了。真可惜。

3.en: WOMAN: I know. I feel the same way.
3.zh: 女士：我知道。我也有同感。

3.en: I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally.
3.zh: 我以前手寫日記，現在則用數位方式寫。

3.en: It just seems less effort to do it that way. So it's not just a problem…
3.zh: 那樣似乎比較省力。所以這不只是個問題……

3.en: That is the end of part three. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part three.
3.zh: 第三部分到此結束。你現在有 30 秒時間檢查第三部分的答案。

4.en: You will hear part of an environmental science lecture about the impact of birds of prey on a farming community in Africa.
4.zh: 你會聽到一段環境科學講座，內容是關於猛禽對非洲一個農業社群的影響。

4.en: First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
4.zh: 首先，你有一些時間閱讀第 31 至 40 題。

4.en: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
4.zh: 現在請仔細聆聽，回答第 31 至 40 題。

4.en: We've been looking at different types of conflicts that may arise between wildlife and humans at the boundaries of protected areas such as national parks and animal sanctuaries.
4.zh: 我們一直在研究野生動物與人類在保護區邊界可能產生的不同衝突，例如國家公園和動物保護區。

4.en: I'd like to illustrate this by telling you about some research that I've been involved in recently in the central African country of Zambia in the area around the Chembe Bird Sanctuary, which contains over three hundred of the listed birds of Zambia.
4.zh: 我想透過我最近參與的一項研究來說明這一點。這項研究位於中非國家尚比亞的 Chembe Bird Sanctuary 周邊地區，該保護區包含超過 300 種尚比亞列名鳥類。

4.en: These include a number of birds of prey, such as eagles, hawks and owls, that live by hunting and killing other birds and animals.
4.zh: 其中包括一些猛禽，例如鷹、隼和貓頭鷹，牠們以捕獵其他鳥類和動物為生。

4.en: Now, most of the people living in the local communities near to the bird sanctuary are small-scale farmers, and these birds of prey provide important social and ecological benefits to them.
4.zh: 現在，住在鳥類保護區附近社區的大多數人都是小規模農民，而這些猛禽為他們提供了重要的社會和生態益處。

4.en: For example, a lot of damage can be caused to farmers' crops by rodents such as rats, which would consume the crops as they grow in the fields as well as after harvesting if they weren't hunted and killed by the birds.
4.zh: 例如，像老鼠這樣的囓齒動物會對農民的作物造成大量損害；如果沒有被鳥類捕食，牠們會在作物生長期間以及收成後吃掉作物。

4.en: And the predatory habits of these birds also protect farmers in other ways.
4.zh: 這些鳥類的捕食習性也在其他方面保護農民。

4.en: For example, a major danger to rural workers is snakes, whose bite may be dangerous or even fatal, and birds of prey have a major role in keeping their populations under control.
4.zh: 例如，蛇是農村工作者面臨的一大危險，蛇咬傷可能很危險，甚至致命；而猛禽在控制蛇的數量方面發揮了重要作用。

4.en: Local people have always been aware of these benefits and for years, even before the sanctuary was opened in 1973, the birds played a key role in the culture of the region.
4.zh: 當地人一直知道這些好處。 多年來，甚至在保護區於 1973 年開放之前，這些鳥類就在該地區文化中扮演關鍵角色。

4.en: However, more recently, the sanctuary and its birds have also become increasingly important to the community in economic terms, because at present, after a relatively slow start, tourism has become an important source of revenue for them.
4.zh: 然而，近年來，這個保護區及其鳥類在經濟層面上對社區也越來越重要，因為目前在起步較慢之後，旅遊業已經成為他們重要的收入來源。

4.en: However, although these birds of prey are protected by the government, their numbers are falling.
4.zh: 然而，雖然這些猛禽受到政府保護，牠們的數量卻正在下降。

4.en: Some of these deaths are accidental. Fatalities occur when birds alight on roads to catch and eat their prey, and are hit by fast-moving traffic.
4.zh: 其中一些死亡是意外造成的。當鳥類降落在道路上捕捉並食用獵物時，可能會被高速行駛的車輛撞死。

4.en: Drivers in Zambia have to take special care at night, as birds may regard the quieter roads as safe places to sleep.
4.zh: 尚比亞的駕駛人在夜間必須特別小心，因為鳥類可能把較安靜的道路視為安全的睡覺地點。

4.en: Accidental deaths may also occur if these birds fly close to high-voltage power lines, as they may be electrocuted.
4.zh: 如果這些鳥飛近高壓電線， 也可能發生意外死亡，因為牠們可能會觸電。

4.en: This is a particular danger in the heavy rain which can occur in the region in the months from December to April.
4.zh: 這在該地區 12 月至 4 月可能出現的大雨期間尤其危險。

4.en: And local farmers also pose a threat to these birds.
4.zh: 當地農民也對這些鳥類構成威脅。

4.en: As well as growing crops, small-scale farmers in the area also rear chickens.
4.zh: 除了種植作物外，當地小規模農民也飼養雞。

4.en: These provide food for the farmers' families, as well as being an important source of income.
4.zh: 這些雞既為農民家庭提供食物，也是重要的收入來源。

4.en: But they're also an easy target for birds of prey, and so farmers may shoot these birds, which is illegal but understandable, or they may poison the birds, which again is illegal and can have negative effects on the ecosystem.
4.zh: 但雞也很容易成為猛禽的獵物，因此農民可能會射殺這些鳥，雖然這是非法的，但可以理解；或者他們可能會毒殺鳥類，這同樣非法，並且可能對生態系統造成負面影響。

4.en: So how else can farmers protect their chickens from birds of prey?
4.zh: 那麼，農民還能如何保護雞不受猛禽攻擊呢？

4.en: Some people believe that to prevent the predators from settling near the area where the chickens are kept it's best to keep this area free from vegetation.
4.zh: 有些人認為，為了防止捕食者停留在養雞區附近，最好清除該區域的植被。

4.en: But in fact this is counter-productive as it means the chickens have no cover to hide in and they'll be easier for the birds to see.
4.zh: 但事實上，這樣做適得其反，因為雞沒有遮蔽物可以躲藏，反而更容易被鳥類看到。

4.en: Another possibility would be to prevent the chickens from going outside at all, and to keep them safe from predators inside a building, but this would cost far too much to be a practical solution.
4.zh: 另一種可能是完全不讓雞到戶外，而是把牠們關在建築物裡以避免被捕食者攻擊， 但這成本太高，無法成為實際可行的解決方案。

4.en: Nearly all the farmers reported that they spent a lot of time and effort trying to frighten off the birds of prey without actually harming them.
4.zh: 幾乎所有農民都表示，他們花了很多時間和精力試圖嚇走猛禽，而不是實際傷害牠們。

4.en: Most of the farmers had at least one dog, and said this was a big help at scaring away the predators.
4.zh: 大多數農民至少養了一條狗，並說這對嚇走捕食者很有幫助。

4.en: Some of the farmers also reported that during the breeding season, when the chickens were particularly vulnerable, they encouraged their children to watch over the chickens and to hit pans with a metal spoon so that the resulting noise would succeed in driving away birds that were trying to seize the young chicks.
4.zh: 一些農民也表示，在繁殖季節，小雞特別脆弱時，他們會鼓勵孩子看顧雞群，並用金屬湯匙敲打鍋子，讓產生的噪音趕走試圖抓走小雞的鳥類。

4.en: None of these methods was a hundred per cent effective, so as a result, the village people told us that rather than just using one method, they were forced to use a combination for them to have any effect.
4.zh: 這些方法沒有一種百分之百有效，因此村民告訴我們， 他們不能只用一種方法，而是必須結合多種方法才會有效。

4.en: And even so, these birds of prey remain a major threat to the chickens' survival and cause considerable economic loss to farmers.
4.zh: 即便如此，這些猛禽仍然是雞群生存的一大威脅，並給農民造成相當大的經濟損失。

4.en: So we looked at the possibility of a longer-term solution to ...
4.zh: 因此，我們開始研究是否有可能找到更長期的解決方案 ……

4.en: That is the end of part four. You now have 1 minute to check your answers to part four.
4.zh: 第四部分到此結束。你現在有一分鐘時間檢查第四部分的答案。

1.explanation: 題目寫：“_____ Hotel on George Street”，要填酒店名稱。 錄音說：“I always recommend people stay at the Kings Hotel.” 後面再確認：“It's actually on George Street.” 所以酒店是 King’s Hotel，而題目已經提供 Hotel，只填 King’s。 中伏位：Murray Station 只是酒店附近的地點，不是酒店名稱。這類專有名詞題要把「名稱」和「位置」分開。

2.explanation: 題目寫：“cost of family room per night: £_____ approx.”，問家庭房每晚大約多少錢。 錄音說： “If you book a family room it's about £125 per night.” “about” 對應題目的 “approx.”；“family room” 和 “per night” 亦完全吻合，所以答案是 125。 中伏位：錄音之後還有 £95，但那是 Sandra 的哥哥最後訂的 double rooms 每間價錢。題目明確問 family room，所以不能填 95。題目已有 £，只寫 125。

3.explanation: 題目寫：“a _____ tour of the city centre, starts in Carlton Square”。 錄音中男士原本提議 “a bus tour”，但 Sandra 隨即說： “I think it's better to do a walking tour.” 後面再補充： “There's one that starts from Carlton Square.” 所以真正推薦的是 walking tour，答案是 walking。 中伏位：bus tour 是男士最初的想法，但被 Sandra 改為 walking tour。這是典型的「先出現干擾答案 → 後面修正」。

4.explanation: 題目寫：“a trip by _____ to the old fort”。 錄音說： “one thing you could do is visit the old fort. You can get there by boat.” 題目和錄音幾乎直接對應，所以答案是 boat。 “by boat” 是交通方式的固定說法，不需要冠詞。

5.explanation: 題目寫 Science Museum 的 “best day to visit”。 錄音先說博物館 “closed on Mondays”，男士再根據親友逗留時間說： “so Tuesday would be best, I think.” “would be best” 直接對應題目的 “best day”，所以答案是 Tuesday。 中伏位：Saturday 亦有被提到，但 Sandra 說 “Saturdays are terrible”，因為很擁擠；Monday 則休館。因此真正的最佳日期是 Tuesday。

6.explanation: 題目寫：“see the exhibition about _____, which opens soon”。 錄音先說舊電腦展 “finished now”，然後 Sandra 說： “There's another one starting soon on space.” “starting soon” = “opens soon”；“on space” = “about space”，所以答案是 space。 中伏位：old computers 是已經結束的展覽；題目控制詞是 opens soon，所以要聽之後的新展覽。

7.explanation: 題目寫 Clacton Market “good for _____ food”。 錄音中男士說： “My cousin's vegetarian – I know it's one of the best places for that kind of food.” 這裡 “that kind of food” 指前面的 vegetarian，所以意思是 Clacton Market 很適合 vegetarian food。 答案是 vegetarian。 中伏位：錄音亦說孩子有 “loads of choice”，但題目問的是特定哪一類 food，而不是選擇是否多。

8.explanation: 題目寫：“need to have lunch before _____ p.m.” 錄音說： “at the weekend most of the stalls stop serving lunch at 2.30.” 如果攤位 2:30 停止供應午餐，就需要在 2:30 p.m. 前吃午餐，所以答案是 2:30。 題目已經印有 p.m.，不用再重複寫。

9.explanation: 題目寫：“save up to _____ % on ticket prices at bargaintickets.com”。 錄音說： “on some seats there's a 75% discount.” “75% discount” 就是最多可節省 75%，所以答案是 75。 題目已經有 %，只需要填數字。

10.explanation: 題目寫 climb Telegraph Hill “to see a view of the _____”。 錄音說： “climb Telegraph Hill – you'll be able to look right down on the port.” “look right down on” 表示從高處俯瞰，所以就是 “see a view of the port”。 答案是 port。 中伏位：Blakewell Gardens 和 Telegraph Hill 都是所在位置；題目問的是登上山後看到甚麼，所以答案不是 gardens 或 hill。

11.explanation: 題目問：帶孩子參觀 stadium 時，speaker 說了哪兩件事。 B — There is a competition for children today 錄音說孩子可以在 café 畫一幅 football-themed drawing： “We'll pick the best one at the end of the afternoon … we'll send your prize.” 會選出最佳作品並送 prize，表示今天有一個給孩子的 competition，所以 B 正確。 C — Parents must stay with their children at all times 錄音提醒家長： “Please don't let your children wander off on their own, even for a minute.” “even for a minute” 表示孩子任何時候都不應自己離開，因此家長要一直陪著，對應 C。 中伏位：A 不對，因為可以拍的是孩子 shooting a penalty，不是與 football player 合照。D 雖然錄音說天氣 hot and sunny，但沒有要求孩子必須帶 sunhats 和 drinks。E 只說推薦 healthy lunch boxes，沒有 special offer。

13.explanation: 題目問：stadium tour 哪兩項 feature 是 new this year。控制詞是 new。 A — VIP tour 錄音說： “you might like to book one of our VIP tours – we've only just started offering these.” “only just started offering” = 最近才開始提供，所以 VIP tours 是新的，答案 A。 C — audio guide 錄音說如果想 self-guided，可以領 headphones 聽 pre-recorded information，然後說： “We've only just introduced this feature.” 這就是 audio guide，而且明確說剛推出，所以答案 C。 中伏位：360 cinema “has been very popular over the years”，明顯不是新項目。Tours in other languages 只是 “thinking of offering … in future”，目前還沒有推出。Dressing room tour 亦沒有說是今年新增。

14.explanation: 題目問：stadium tour 哪兩項 feature 是 new this year。控制詞是 new。 A — VIP tour 錄音說： “you might like to book one of our VIP tours – we've only just started offering these.” “only just started offering” = 最近才開始提供，所以 VIP tours 是新的，答案 A。 C — audio guide 錄音說如果想 self-guided，可以領 headphones 聽 pre-recorded information，然後說： “We've only just introduced this feature.” 這就是 audio guide，而且明確說剛推出，所以答案 C。 中伏位：360 cinema “has been very popular over the years”，明顯不是新項目。Tours in other languages 只是 “thinking of offering … in future”，目前還沒有推出。Dressing room tour 亦沒有說是今年新增。

15.explanation: 題目年份是 1870。 錄音說： “1870 was also the year that football teams started to include a player whose role it was to guard the goal.” 負責守住球門的球員就是 goalkeeper，所以這一年發生的是 the introduction of goalkeepers。 答案是 D。

16.answer: F — two changes to the rules of the game
16.explanation: 題目年份是 1874。 錄音說 1874 年有兩項規則改變： “referees were allowed to send players off if they committed certain offences.” 以及： “teams started having to swap ends at half-time.” 一項是容許裁判把球員罰出場，另一項是半場交換場地，因此正好是 two changes to the rules of the game。 答案是 F。 中伏位：題目不是要選其中一項具體規則，要匹配選項中對這一年整體事件的概括。

17.answer: B — a change to the design of the goal
17.explanation: 題目年份是 1875。 錄音說以前球門頂端用 tape 連接： “In 1875, that tape was replaced with the solid crossbar that we're familiar with today.” 由 tape 改成 solid crossbar，就是改變了 goal 的設計。 所以答案是 B。

18.answer: H — an agreement on the length of a game
18.explanation: 題目年份是 1877。 錄音說： “all the clubs decided to set a limit of ninety minutes for each match.” 即各球會正式同意每場比賽限制為 90 分鐘，所以對應： an agreement on the length of a game 答案是 H。 中伏位：錄音亦提到當年有更多 clubs founded，但選項問的是 football 發展的重要事件；真正有對應選項的是統一比賽時間。

19.answer: C — the first use of lights for matches
19.explanation: 題目年份是 1878。 錄音說： “In addition, referees started using whistles, and electric lamps were installed on certain pitches.” 這讓： “games could then be played in the evenings all year round.” electric lamps 安裝在球場上，即開始利用燈光進行比賽，所以答案是 C — the first use of lights for matches。 中伏位：whistles 也在同一年開始使用，但選項沒有 whistles；真正能與選項配對的是 electric lamps。

20.answer: G — the introduction of a fee for spectators
20.explanation: 題目年份是 1880。 錄音說： “In 1880, clubs began to charge fans for admission to games.” “charge fans for admission” 就是要求 spectators 付入場費，所以對應： the introduction of a fee for spectators 答案是 G。 中伏位：錄音接著說 players “were still amateurs”，所以這一年並不是開始付薪給球員。A 不對。

21.explanation: 題目問：學習 handwriting 對兒童的哪些好處，兩位學生都覺得意外。所以每個答案都要證明兩個人都 surprised。 C — improved concentration 男士說： “What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration.” 女士回應： “That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before.” 男士覺得這個好處不明顯；女士也說以前從沒想到。兩人都覺得意外，所以 C 正確。 E — improved spatial awareness 男士說： “I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either.” 女士回答： “I thought that too.” 即兩人原本都沒有把 handwriting 和 spatial awareness 聯想到一起，所以 E 正確。 中伏位：memory 對女士來說 “seems pretty obvious”；imagination 她說 “I would've guessed that”，都不是令兩人意外。Fine motor skills 更是女士 “I'd always assumed” 的好處。

22.explanation: 題目問：學習 handwriting 對兒童的哪些好處，兩位學生都覺得意外。所以每個答案都要證明兩個人都 surprised。 C — improved concentration 男士說： “What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration.” 女士回應： “That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before.” 男士覺得這個好處不明顯；女士也說以前從沒想到。兩人都覺得意外，所以 C 正確。 E — improved spatial awareness 男士說： “I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either.” 女士回答： “I thought that too.” 即兩人原本都沒有把 handwriting 和 spatial awareness 聯想到一起，所以 E 正確。 中伏位：memory 對女士來說 “seems pretty obvious”；imagination 她說 “I would've guessed that”，都不是令兩人意外。Fine motor skills 更是女士 “I'd always assumed” 的好處。

23.explanation: 題目問：對 dyspraxia 兒童而言，哪兩種 handwriting problem 是學生認為 easiest to correct。控制詞是 easiest，所以要找他們認為有簡單解決方法的問題。 A — not spacing letters correctly 女士說： “One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper.” 然後： “that trains them to space the letters correctly.” “simple thing” 表示這問題相對容易處理，而 grid paper 可直接訓練 letter spacing，因此答案 A。 C — applying too much pressure when writing 女士說： “I liked the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard.” 接著評價： “That seems like a really simple solution.” press too hard = applying too much pressure；而 “really simple solution” 直接說明它容易糾正，所以答案 C。 中伏位：letter shapes 需要 “lots of games” 和 “a lot of patience”，並不容易。Writing slowly 更被男士說 “I'm not sure there's much you can do”，所以也不是 easiest。

24.explanation: 題目問：對 dyspraxia 兒童而言，哪兩種 handwriting problem 是學生認為 easiest to correct。控制詞是 easiest，所以要找他們認為有簡單解決方法的問題。 A — not spacing letters correctly 女士說： “One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper.” 然後： “that trains them to space the letters correctly.” “simple thing” 表示這問題相對容易處理，而 grid paper 可直接訓練 letter spacing，因此答案 A。 C — applying too much pressure when writing 女士說： “I liked the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard.” 接著評價： “That seems like a really simple solution.” press too hard = applying too much pressure；而 “really simple solution” 直接說明它容易糾正，所以答案 C。 中伏位：letter shapes 需要 “lots of games” 和 “a lot of patience”，並不容易。Writing slowly 更被男士說 “I'm not sure there's much you can do”，所以也不是 easiest。

25.answer: C — Children react more positively if they make a mistake
25.explanation: 題目問：女士怎樣看用 laptop 教 dyslexia 兒童 writing。 錄音說： “It's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong – on a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go.” 即使用 keyboard 時，即使犯錯也較少挫敗，孩子更願意繼續嘗試，所以對應： react more positively if they make a mistake 答案是 C。 中伏位：女士之後明確說 “developing fluency isn't any faster”，所以 B 不對。A 亦相反，因為她說孩子會 “more willing to have a go”。

26.answer: A — cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children
26.explanation: 題目問女士在 cursive 與 print writing 之間的看法。 錄音說： “it's been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn – especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.” 所以 cursive 對某一特定群體——children with learning difficulties——更加困難，即令他們處於不利位置。 因此答案是 A。 中伏位：錄音說 cursive 過去被認為 stylish and educated，但 “not anymore”；沒有說 print writing 與較低成績有關，也沒有說英國大部分老師仍偏好傳統 cursive。

27.answer: A — There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting
27.explanation: 題目問 poor handwriting 對 exam performance 有甚麼影響。 男士說自己以前擔心字跡影響成績，然後說： “now research shows that I was right to worry.” 女士再補充： “Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script.” research + marks affected 直接證明 poor handwriting 會影響 grades，所以答案是 A。 中伏位：題目不是問學生是否覺得這樣 unfair；題目問實際對 exam performance 的 impact。錄音明確有研究證據支持。

28.answer: B — Children will continue to learn to write by hand
28.explanation: 題目問男士對 handwriting 未來的預測。 女士問： “Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future?” 男士回答： “I can't see that changing much.” 後面又說： “teachers understand the value of handwriting. It's a basic life skill.” 意思是他認為 handwriting 仍會保持重要，兒童仍然會學習手寫，所以答案是 B。 中伏位：他提到 touch typing “still isn't taught in most schools”，不是預測未來會在 handwriting 前先教； 反而說將來甚至可能直接在 digital devices 上手寫。

29.explanation: 題目問女士擔心：依賴 digital devices 令她自己哪方面變得困難。 錄音說： “my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent.” 她接著說： “I think you can put that down to lack of practice.” put that down to = 歸因於；她認為少了手寫練習導致拼字與標點能力變差。 所以答案是 B — spell and punctuate。 中伏位：note taking 和 reading historical documents 都有被男士／女士提到，但她真正用自己的情況表達擔憂的是 spelling 和 punctuation。

30.answer: C — regretful that they have lost the habit
30.explanation: 題目問兩位學生對自己的 handwriting 有甚麼感受。 男士說： “Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now.” 又說自己的 handwriting 已經沒有人能認出： “It's a shame.” 女士回應： “I feel the same way. I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally.” 兩人都懷念以前手寫的習慣，並對自己現在幾乎不再手寫感到可惜，所以答案是 C — regretful that they have lost the habit。 中伏位：他們沒有說自己寫得慢，也沒有因別人的批評而 embarrassed；重點是 miss / used to / hardly ever now / it's a shame。

31.explanation: 題目寫： “They destroy _____ and other rodents.” 錄音說農作物會被： “rodents such as rats” 破壞，如果沒有猛禽捕食，牠們會吃掉田裡及收割後的 crops。 題目已經把 rats 歸入 broader category “rodents”，所以： rats and other rodents 答案是 rats。 因為 “other rodents” 表示空格本身也是一種 rodent。

32.explanation: 題目寫： “They help to prevent farmers from being bitten by _____.” 錄音說： “a major danger to rural workers is snakes, whose bite may be dangerous or even fatal” 而 birds of prey： “have a major role in keeping their populations under control.” 控制 snakes 數量 → 農民被蛇咬的風險下降，所以答案是 snakes。

33.explanation: 題目寫： “They now support the economy by encouraging _____ in the area.” 錄音說近年保護區與鳥類在經濟方面愈來愈重要： “because … tourism has become an important source of revenue for them.” “source of revenue” 表示為社區帶來收入，所以 birds support the economy through tourism。 答案是 tourism。 中伏位：題目用 “encouraging” 改寫錄音的因果關係，並不是要求錄音一定出現 “encourage tourism” 這個完整搭配。

34.explanation: 題目寫 birds may accidentally be killed: “by _____ when they are hunting or sleeping.” 錄音先說鳥為捕食而落到道路上時： “are hit by fast-moving traffic.” 之後又說夜間鳥可能把安靜的道路當成睡覺地方。 所以無論 hunting 或 sleeping，危險來源都是道路上的 traffic。 答案是 traffic。 中伏位：drivers 有被提到，但真正「撞死」鳥的是 fast-moving traffic；題目也要求 ONE WORD ONLY。

35.explanation: 題目寫： “electrocution from contact with power lines, especially at times when there is a lot of _____.” 錄音說： “This is a particular danger in the heavy rain which can occur … from December to April.” “heavy rain” = a lot of rain，所以答案是 rain。 題目已經有 “a lot of”，因此只需要不可數名詞 rain，不填 heavy。

36.explanation: 題目寫： “Local farmers may illegally shoot them or _____ them.” 錄音說： “farmers may shoot these birds, which is illegal … or they may poison the birds, which again is illegal.” 題目直接保留 shoot，第二個動作就是 poison。 答案是 poison。 文法上空格位於 “may … them”，所以需要原形動詞 poison。

37.explanation: 題目在保護 chickens 的方法中寫： “providing a _____ for chickens, expensive” 錄音說另一方法是： “prevent the chickens from going outside at all, and to keep them safe from predators inside a building” 但： “this would cost far too much to be a practical solution.” inside a building → providing a building；cost far too much → expensive。 所以答案是 building。 中伏位：題目不是問 keep chickens indoors 這個動作，題目問需要提供甚麼實體設施。

38.explanation: 題目寫 frightening birds of prey by: “keeping a _____” 錄音說： “Most of the farmers had at least one dog, and said this was a big help at scaring away the predators.” “scaring away” = frightening，所以其中一種方法就是養一隻 dog。 題目前已有 a，所以填單數名詞 dog。

39.explanation: 題目寫 frightening birds of prey by: “making a _____, e.g. with metal objects” 錄音說孩子會： “hit pans with a metal spoon so that the resulting noise would succeed in driving away birds” 用金屬物件敲打 → 產生 noise → 趕走猛禽，所以答案是 noise。 中伏位：pans / metal spoon 是製造聲音的工具；題目空格問的是 making a _____，即製造出來的東西，因此是 noise。

40.explanation: 題目寫： “A _____ of methods is usually most effective.” 錄音說： “rather than just using one method, they were forced to use a combination for them to have any effect.” “rather than just one method” 強調單一方法不足；需要把多種方法結合。 所以： a combination of methods 答案是 combination。 中伏位：錄音亦明確說 “None of these methods was a hundred per cent effective”，因此不是某一個方法最好，多種方法合併使用最有效。
